started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to know about the child (or children) you're claiming for.

**Could you tell me:**
1. How many children are you asking about?
2. What are their names?
3. How old is each child?

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 5 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! So you're asking about your son Alex, who is 5 years old.

Since Alex is under 16, he falls into the automatic qualification age category. Now let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex is only 5 years old, he wouldn't be working. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question: **Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

(For a 5-year-old, this would be very unusual, so I expect the answer is no, but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's only 5!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: You're absolutely right! At 5 years old, that would be very unusual. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Again, since Alex is only 5 years old, he wouldn't be in any apprenticeship. Let me move to the next step.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. **Do you normally live in the UK?**

Or if not, do any of these special circumstances apply to you:
- You have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You're living abroad as a Crown servant
- You're in certain other qualifying situations

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Living in Manchester means you meet the UK residency requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to confirm: **Are you responsible for Alex?**

This means either:
- You live with Alex, OR
- You contribute to his upkeep (paying for things like food, clothes, housing, etc. at least equal to the Child Benefit amount)

Do either of these apply to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex lives with you, you're clearly responsible for him. Let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to ask: **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example, another parent, grandparent, or someone else who looks after him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's living situation. **Is Alex:**
- Currently in hospital?
- In local authority care?
- Being fostered?
- Or living normally at home with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living normally at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! One final question: **Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

(This would typically apply if the council was providing financial support for his care or housing costs)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards his care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

**For your son Alex**, you meet all the eligibility requirements:
- ✅ Alex is 5 years old (under 16)
- ✅ He's not working or receiving benefits in his own right
- ✅ You live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ You're responsible for Alex (he lives with you)
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- ✅ Alex lives at home with you
- ✅ The local council isn't paying towards his care

**Next Steps to Claim:**

1. **Apply** - You can apply online or by post using form CH2
2. **Provide proof** - You'll need:
   - Proof of identity for yourself and Alex
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
3. **Payments** - Child Benefit is usually paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

**Important Note:** Be aware of the **High Income Child Benefit Charge** if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year. You can still claim, but may need to pay back some or all of the benefit through your tax return.

You can start your claim here: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Do you have any questions about the application process?
